questions.prompt: Where is YOU with the puck?
questions.explanation: The puck is behind the left goal line, so YOU can use the net to change Gold 1’s angle; if Gold 1 follows, outlet picture changes.

questions.prompt: Which two facts make behind-net space useful?

options.text: Gold 1 is above the goal line
The puck is already at centre ice

questions.explanation: Gold 1’s higher position leaves a route and D2 can connect middle; centre ice is not scene state.

questions.prompt: Arrange one behind-net escape.

options.text: Carry behind net with puck protected
Recheck D2 and W before exiting

questions.explanation: Pressure side sets route; the net can screen the carry; final scan selects exit.

questions.prompt: Move D2 into a low-middle outlet lane below Gold 1.
questions.explanation: The low-middle spot gives YOU a short option after the carry and keeps W separate; if Gold 1 drops inside, D2 re-angles.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 follows behind the net, what deserves a fresh read?

options.text: Whether W is now far-side outlet and D2 inside support

questions.explanation: Gold 1’s route changes pressure side, so compare W and D2; if both covered, protect and wait.

questions.prompt: How does the net change the forechecker’s approach without guaranteeing an exit?
questions.explanation: The net makes Gold 1 turn and may reveal support, but a pass is safe only if the support lane is visible; if lanes stay covered, keep possession.

scenarios.title: Delay the entry until support arrives
scenarios.objective: Use a controlled delay to let support arrive at a different lane
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. F1 carries over the left blue line but slows with Gold 1 in middle. YOU trails right; D2 joins late.
cues: F1 slowed at the left blue line; Gold 1 shades middle.
YOU trails right and D2 joins late.

questions.prompt: What has F1 done before this freeze?
questions.explanation: F1’s slowed carrier gives support time, but delay does not guarantee a lane; if Gold 1 closes space, update.

questions.prompt: Which two things help YOU stay useful during the delay?

options.text: Remain at a different height from F1
Keep a route back toward puck
Rush past F1 into same lane

questions.explanation: Different height and connected route give F1 another option; rushing past removes delay’s purpose.

questions.prompt: Order one delayed-entry support.

options.text: Arrive when F1 can see connection

questions.explanation: Gold 1 sets open side; separation preserves lane; arriving visibly turns delay into support.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to an outside-lower support pocket behind F1.
questions.explanation: The pocket gives F1 a release behind Gold 1 and keeps D2 separate; if Gold 1 follows, rotate toward D2.

questions.prompt: If F1 loses control during the delay, what must you reassess first?

options.text: Where the new puck threat is and whether support becomes recovery
Calling for a pass from a player without puck

questions.explanation: A bobble changes entry support to recovery, so locate puck and danger; if F1 regains it, rebuild support.

questions.prompt: What does saving ice mean in this particular scene?
questions.explanation: It means staying connected and separated while F1 waits for D2, preserving a route to use or recover through; if delay removes support, it became a problem.

scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. W carries below the left dot. Gold 1 and Gold 2 occupy the slot; YOU is high middle and D2 is weak-side point.
cues: W has puck below the left dot.
Gold 1 and Gold 2 occupy slot; YOU are high middle.

questions.prompt: What is crowded in this freeze?
questions.explanation: Both Gold defenders occupy the slot, so a direct middle pass is restricted; if one leaves, reset picture changes.

questions.prompt: Which two reset cues are visible?

options.text: Both Navy players are below goal line

questions.explanation: High separation and weak-side support give W outlets away from slot; low crowding would leave no reset.

questions.prompt: Arrange one crowded-slot reset.
questions.explanation: Defenders explain why slot is closed; high support preserves possession; reentry waits for a new lane.

questions.prompt: Move YOU higher and slightly left to show a reset lane from W.
questions.explanation: The high-left pocket opens a pass away from both slot defenders and leaves D2 intact; if Gold 1 follows, D2 may become reset.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 follows YOU high, what might help W?

options.text: Use D2’s weak-side lane while Gold 2 remains slot

questions.explanation: Gold 1’s movement can uncover D2, so use changed coverage; if D2 covered, protect and wait.

questions.prompt: Why is a reset a positive action here?
questions.explanation: It moves possession from two slot defenders and preserves an attack after coverage shifts; if high lane is covered too, keeping puck beats forcing.

scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. Navy leads late. YOU controls puck on left wall; W is changing, D2 is safe support, and Gold 1 closes middle.
cues: The late lead and change are stated objectives.
Gold 1 closes middle; D2 is behind YOU on wall side.

questions.prompt: Which two cues support a wall-side hold?

questions.prompt: Arrange one change-management read.

options.text: Use D2 or wait until W is ready

questions.explanation: Pressure tells you where not to force; wall protection buys time; D2 or delayed release keeps change connected.

questions.prompt: Move D2 closer to YOU on the wall-side support lane.
questions.explanation: Closer wall support gives YOU a short connection while middle is covered; if Gold 1 follows, protect and wait.

questions.prompt: If middle opens before W returns, what can change?

questions.prompt: Why is a safe-side hold a decision rather than a default?
questions.explanation: It fits lead, change, pressure and D2 support, but a new lane or lost support changes the choice; puck and teammates still need reading.

options.text: YOU retrieve if lane is reachable

questions.prompt: Move D1 between Gold 1 and the Navy net while YOU attacks wall puck.

questions.prompt: Why is a failed clear a role-change moment?

findings.issue: Every new-scene briefing uses '+x' and '-x' axis notation in player-facing text. U13 players should receive named-net language.
findings.evidence: All 25 exp26b-u13 briefings begin with 'Navy attacks the +x end and Gold attacks the -x end.'
findings.recommendedChange: Replace that sentence in each new briefing with 'Navy attacks Gold's net and defends Navy's net.' Preserve the actual net and actor geometry while removing coordinate notation from the player-facing scene.

findings.issue: The listed distractors are unrelated trivia, impossible guarantees, or automatic-certainty claims rather than credible U13 hockey decisions.
findings.evidence: Examples include 'The original faceoff result', 'Whether the bench door is open', 'The score from a previous game', 'A guaranteed open net', 'That the shot must go in', 'The goalie’s save is guaranteed', 'Changed teams', and 'The neutral-zone bench'.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace each affected distractor with a plausible nearby choice involving pressure route, support lane, puck protection, coverage handoff, or a conditional branch in that scene. Avoid guaranteed outcomes, irrelevant bench/game trivia, and choices that no player could reasonably select in the shown play.
